Full ODE-system comparison (child vs parent, 200 time points over t in [0, 100]) shows the new Allee term drives the target trajectory by up to 157.5 units (~315x sigma=0.5), strongest near t≈5.5 where prey abundance sits near the Allee threshold. All other parent terms remain physically active on the same trajectory (logistic growth ~0.5*N up to 0.5*100=50, Type-II predation of order tens, aggregation-defense saturating near 3.0). New-term visibility easily exceeds the 5*sigma bar.</excitation_report>
<parameter name="rationale">Standard predator-prey system with logistic growth, Type-II Beddington-DeAngelis functional response, crowding-defense saturating term, and the newly added Allee-effect term. Roles confirmed against the ODE contract: t is the sole independent axis; N, P are dynamic states; every other symbol is a fixed parameter. Chose K=100 to bracket the N(0)=40 initial condition, r=0.5/yr for a modest herbivore, handling_time=0.5 and predation_rate=0.02 for saturating intake, predator_interference=0.05 for mild mutual interference, conversion=0.3 and death=0.1 to sustain limit-cycle behavior. Allee parameters chosen inside the suggested band (strength=0.8, threshold=10) so the Allee effect bites once prey dip near/below 10 during the trough of the cycle — this is exactly the regime where the new mechanism differs from the parent equation.</rationale>
